title: Google Meet Screen Share Not Working: How to Fix It
body_md:
![Google Meet Help page on presenting during a video meeting](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/google-meet-screen-share-not-working-how-to-fix-it/1.png)
*Google's official Present during a video meeting help page ([source](https://support.google.com/meet/answer/9308856))*

On a Mac, a missing screen-recording permission can prevent sharing. If you missed the permission prompt, check **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording** for the browser, then quit and reopen it before rejoining. If the Present option is missing or disabled, the host or a Workspace admin may have restricted sharing — Google's own documentation says sharing your screen may be disabled for you due to admin settings or meeting host controls. See [Google's presentation guidance](https://support.google.com/meet/answer/9308856).

## Why This Happens

Screen sharing breaks in Meet for a handful of predictable reasons:

- **Missing OS-level screen recording permission.** macOS blocks apps from capturing your display until you explicitly allow it, and the permission only takes effect after the browser restarts.
- **Permissions that "look" enabled but aren't.** After a macOS or Chrome update, an already-on toggle can stop working and needs to be removed and re-added.
- **The host turned sharing off.** Meeting hosts can stop participants from sharing their screen, and that control requires Host Management to be turned on. When sharing is off, the Present option simply isn't available to you.
- **Wrong entry point.** If you click Present in the green room before joining, you join in Companion mode — and your mic and speaker are unavailable in that mode.
- **No audio in the share.** This isn't broken sharing, it's the wrong share type. To share audio from your presentation, you have to present a tab and toggle on "Also share tab audio."
- **Browser or extension conflicts.** Old browser builds, aggressive privacy extensions, or Meet-specific extensions can block the capture prompt.

## Step-by-Step Fixes

### 1. Grant (or reset) screen recording permission on macOS

Google's guidance for permission prompts: when you start a presentation or recording in a meeting, click Allow in the dialog — and if you missed that dialog, you'll need to update your system settings. Google calls this out specifically for macOS Sequoia, where you get a cautionary prompt the first time you try to record or share your screen.

1. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording** (older macOS: System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Privacy → Screen Recording).
2. Toggle on your browser or the Google Meet app. If it's not listed, use the **+** button to add it.
3. Authenticate with your password or Touch ID if prompted.
4. Choose **Quit & Reopen** when macOS asks. The permission won't apply until the browser fully restarts.
5. Rejoin the meeting and try **Present now** again.

**If the toggle was already on and sharing still fails:** select the browser, hit the **–** button to remove it, then add it back and restart. macOS updates can leave this permission in a stale state.

### 2. Check host controls

If the Present button is missing or grayed out for you but works for others, the host has locked sharing. A host or co-host can fix it in seconds: join the meeting, click **Host controls** at the bottom right, and in the side panel toggle **Share their screen** on. On mobile, tap the screen, tap More, tap **Host controls**, and turn **Share their screen** on or off at the bottom.

If you're not the host, message them in chat — you can't override this yourself. Asking to be made a co-host works too.

### 3. Make sure you actually joined the meeting

Don't click Present from the pre-join screen unless you mean to. Clicking Present in the green room puts you in Companion mode, where your mic and speaker are unavailable. Join the meeting normally first, then share.

### 4. Use the right share type

At the bottom, click **Present now** (newer builds label it **Share screen**), then pick **Your entire screen**, **A window**, or **Chrome Tab**. A few gotchas:

- **Video or audio playback?** Share a **tab**, not the whole screen, and turn on **Also share tab audio**.
- **Multiple monitors?** "Your entire screen" asks you to pick *one* display. Pick the one your content is actually on.
- **Someone else presenting?** Choose **Present instead** — starting your presentation pauses theirs.

### 5. Swap or reset the browser

Meet's deepest integration is with Chrome, and Firefox and Safari work but drop the occasional feature. Try, in order:

1. Fully quit and reopen the browser (not just close the tab).
2. Update to the latest version.
3. Disable extensions — ad blockers, privacy tools, and Meet add-ons are common offenders.
4. Test in an incognito/private window with extensions off.
5. Try a different profile or a different browser to isolate the problem.

### 6. Rule out the network and the stop button

If you're clearly presenting on your end but attendees see a frozen or black screen, bandwidth is one possible cause, not a diagnosis. Turn off your camera, close bandwidth-heavy apps, switch from Wi-Fi to Ethernet if you can, or stop and restart the share. To stop cleanly, click **Stop Presenting**, or click **You are presenting** in the bottom right and choose **Stop presenting**.

### 7. Ask your admin

If nothing works and you're on a work or school account, sharing may be disabled at the organization level. Admins have a Present setting that allows users to share their screen, and if it's off, users can't share — even in meetings hosted by other organizations. Your IT admin can confirm and change it.

## How to Prevent It Next Time

- **Grant the macOS permission before you need it.** Check it before important meetings and recheck after major OS updates.
- **Re-check permissions after big OS updates.** These toggles can reset or go stale.
- **Do a 30-second dry run** before any important demo — join a solo meeting from your own link and test Present now.
- **Keep a clean browser profile for meetings** with extensions kept to a minimum.
- **If you host recurring calls,** check your host controls once and confirm **Share their screen** is on.

## My Take

My read is that most "Meet screen share not working" cases are two problems wearing one costume: a macOS permission that never got granted, or a host toggle you can't see. Both of those are binary. If Present is grayed out, stop troubleshooting your network — it's a permissions question, not a bandwidth one.

I think the macOS permission reset is the single most underrated fix. Removing the browser from the Screen & System Audio Recording list and adding it back clears a stale state that an already-green toggle hides, and it costs you one browser restart. That's cheaper than reinstalling Chrome, which is what most people try third.

The fair point on the other side: Google's documentation is genuinely decent here, and a lot of this is spelled out in the help page if you read past the first screen. The problem is that nobody reads support docs while twelve people wait on a call. That's the real failure, not the product.

If you present for a living, I'd do the 30-second dry run before anything that matters, especially the first time after a macOS update. The permission dialogs changed with Sequoia, and the failure always shows up at the worst moment.
